name: go-to-shortcuts
title: Go-to shortcuts
description: Two-key navigation like G then I: press the prefix and a small panel lists where each letter goes, so the first press teaches the keys.
docs: Pass destinations ({ key, label, href, onGo }): onGo wins, and href loads the address. After the prefix (g by default) a hint panel appears at the bottom left of the window, listing each key with its label; the next key goes there, and Escape, any other key, a click or the timeout (1500 ms, shown as a bar running down along the foot of the panel) puts the panel away. The listener ignores presses in text fields, selects and editable areas, inside dialogs, with Ctrl, Cmd, Alt or Shift on the prefix, and while a key is held down. A screen reader hears Go to: press a letter, politely, and Going to Inbox after. scope is a ref to an element: only presses from inside it count, for a region of an app; leave it out to listen to the whole page. enabled turns it off. The panel is fixed, and className moves it, for example className="absolute bottom-3 left-3" inside a relative region. GoToHint is the same panel drawn on its own, to teach the keys in a help page. goToShortcut(key, prefix) from the item's shortcuts file returns { aria-keyshortcuts } for links you draw yourself: ARIA has no syntax for a sequence, so the value is the keys in order, g i. labels translates every word.
